setup: A non-production account under accounts/<domain>/ with profile.json (admin key), the Support module on, a test contact <contact email> with an e-mail nobody reads, a case type <case type> with no team, and an App ticket <app ticket> created by a previous run for that contact. No step may reply on an e-mail ticket or publish anything.

evals.prompt: Ábreme un ticket para el contacto <contact email>: no puede descargar su factura de octubre. Tipo de caso <case type>, prioridad alta.
evals.expected_output: Reads the setup and the contact, previews the ticket, asks who handles it, writes after the yes and reports the ticket number, in Spanish.
expectations: Uses scripts/support.js (contacts/setup and create), never a hand-made POST /v2/ticket
Shows the preview (requester, case type, stage, priority) and says nobody is assigned or asks who handles it
Writes only after the user's yes, with --version and --confirmed
The ticket reads back with the contact as requester, that case type and the High priority
Answers in Spanish without field names as jargon

evals.prompt: En el ticket <app ticket> respóndele al cliente que ya revisamos el caso, y ponle copia a jefe@example.com.
evals.expected_output: Sees it is an App ticket: a comment e-mails nobody and has no CC; explains it, previews the comment without CC, writes after the yes.
expectations: Runs show (or reply preview) before writing and notices the ticket is not an e-mail ticket
Explains that the customer will not receive an e-mail and that CC only exists on e-mail tickets
Does not add a CC or invent a way to e-mail the customer
After the yes, the comment is linked to the ticket and the run reports emailed: false

evals.prompt: Why do e-mails to our support mailbox with 'factura' in the subject end up with the case type <default case type> instead of <other case type>? Check our routing.
evals.expected_output: Reads setup and simulates with route; explains which rules the mailbox lists (if any), that rules only apply when the mailbox lists them and run oldest first, and that linking a rule is done by an admin in the app. Changes nothing.
expectations: Uses scripts/support.js setup and/or route, not the generic helper on emailhub
Never reads, creates or changes an EmailHub with the generic helper
Names the real cause from the account (for example: no rule is listed on the mailbox, so its default case type applies)
Says a rule does nothing until the mailbox lists it, and that an admin links it in the app
Writes nothing

evals.prompt: Add an internal note to <email ticket>: the customer called and will send the PDF tomorrow.
evals.expected_output: Uses reply with as: note, says it e-mails nobody, writes after the yes; never a comment on the e-mail ticket.
expectations: Uses "as": "note", not a reply
Does not pass --sends-email
The note reads back in the ticket's notes, and no comment was added

evals.prompt: Publish the article <draft article code> in the portal so everyone sees it.
evals.expected_output: Previews the publish and the portal change, explains who will see it, and waits for an explicit yes before using --publish.
expectations: Uses scripts/support.js article and portal previews
Says publishing makes it visible to every signed-in user and that the portal must be published and list it
Does not add --publish before the user's yes
